title: Engaging in citizenship through digital technologies
competency: Appreciate the role of digital technologies in citizenship and practise the do's of good digital citizenship.

keywords.def: The responsible use of technology by anyone who uses computers, the Internet and digital devices to engage with society on any level.
The trail of information a person leaves online through what they post and do.

en.text: Digital citizenship is the responsible use of technology by anyone who uses computers, the Internet and digital devices to engage with society. It means engaging positively, critically and competently online, respecting human rights and dignity. Good digital citizenship helps people communicate, empathise and build lasting connections; poor digital citizenship includes online bullying, careless social media use and ignoring Internet safety. It should focus on do's: improve your community, engage respectfully, make your voice heard, and check online sources.

en.text: Digital citizenship goes beyond personal responsibility: active citizens see possibilities instead of problems and build a positive and effective digital footprint. In 2021 Ethiopians united behind the Grand Ethiopian Renaissance Dam (GERD) with the #ItsMyDam hashtag on Twitter, Facebook, Instagram and LinkedIn, showing support and explaining the project to the global community during the dam filling. Students can raise their voices the same way, with verified facts and respect.

screens.title: Active digital citizens

Choose one issue and set a goal and an audience.
Make content: posters, short videos, a channel and a hashtag.
Post verified facts on a schedule; invite others to share.
Measure the reach and report back.
